summary: Currency converter takes an amount in one currency and shows what it comes to in another, with the exchange rate underneath. Each side has a menu to pick a currency, and a swap button flips the two while keeping the same amount of money. It helps people outside your home market understand what a plan or an agent run will cost them.
use: When a pricing or billing page should show plan prices in a buyer's local currency
When an agent quotes a cost and the person wants to see it in their own currency
When you have your own exchange rates and need a small converter to display them
When people should see the rate and how recently it was updated
features: The converted amount rolls to each new value as the amount or currencies change.
Each side opens a menu of `currencies` with code and name, and the current one is checked.
Picking the currency already on the other side moves that side to a different currency, so the two never match.
Swap flips the currencies and carries the converted amount into the amount field.
The rate line reads like "1 USD = 0.9200 EUR", followed by the `updated` text.
Each currency sets its own `symbol`, `rate` against the base and `decimals`, such as 0 for yen, and `locale` sets the thousands separators.
a11y: The amount input is labelled Amount and opens a decimal keypad on touch devices.
Currency menus use `role="menu"` with `menuitemradio` items and `aria-checked` on the selected currency.
The currency buttons report `aria-expanded`, and Escape closes an open menu and returns focus to its button.
The icon-only swap button has the label "Swap currencies" and a tooltip.

faq.q: Where do the exchange rates come from?
faq.a: From you. The component never fetches rates. Pass `currencies` with a `rate` for each, measured against a base currency whose rate is 1, and set `updated` to say how fresh they are.

faq.q: Why does the amount change when I press swap?
faq.a: Swap keeps the money the same. The converted amount becomes the new amount, so 24 USD shown as 22.08 EUR becomes 22.08 EUR converting back to USD.

faq.q: How do I show yen without decimals?
faq.a: Set `decimals: 0` on that currency. The built-in list already does this for JPY.
